notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b (head 74112b4, uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript carries the tier's model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (tool calls are Read, Write, Edit and Bash), no transcript mentions SKILL.md, ex_unit.md or processes.md, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line (Do not invoke any skills.) requires; skills_listed is 209. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex. opus-1 also wrote a mutation-check script outside its run folder and haiku-2 a probe at /tmp/probe_test.exs; neither is in files and neither is graded.

Changes since 0814e8d (git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the eleven rules this case's index rows name, two changed, both about for. The other nine are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-31 standard; the diff's changes to macros.md and to an example in processes.md touch none of them.

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (changed): the sentence "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." and its example are gone. "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" (changed) adds a `for`'s generators and filters to the selections and now decides the shape: "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line, and a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes in `do ... end`." This decides one construct in the five files: sonnet-2 line 128 for pid <- pids, do: Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", pid), clean under both rules. Under the old sentence it would have made sonnet-2 violate the do: rule. The sonnet-2 for blocks at lines 86-88 (the one-line form would run to 122 columns) and 120-126 (holds a fn) are clean under the same sentence. No other run has a for on do:; opus-1's line 142 for is a block holding a test.

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else": 1 of 5 violates. sonnet-1 line 180 pid = spawn(fn -> receive do: (:crash -> exit(:boom)) end) writes a receive on do:, the shape 2026-10-31 graded violated, decided by "A body of several sequential expressions, or one that holds a construct with a structure of its own, a `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`, a comment, or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is". Clean constructs: opus-1 241 and 245, sonnet-1 44, sonnet-2 9 and 47; opus-1 line 16 if String.starts_with?(to, "rejected"), do: {:error, :rejected}, else: :ok has a plain condition and two literal branches. haiku-1 and haiku-2 have no do: at all and write every body holding a fn or receive as a block, graded clean as before.

"One expression per line, and tabular clauses": 2 of 5 violate. sonnet-1 line 180 puts a receive on the fn's line, the shape 2026-10-31 graded violated. sonnet-2 line 53 true -> Process.sleep(10) && wait_until(fun, attempts - 1) is a judgment call on a shape this rule has not graded (earlier sweeps quoted the same line only under Wait, before this rule existed). It is one expression by syntax, but Process.sleep/1 always returns :ok, so && does not choose anything: it sequences two steps to keep them on the -> line. The rule says "What asks for a second line is not a second call but a second expression: a body of several sequential expressions", and the rows are not a table, since "Clauses are not a table when they do different kinds of work, as when one row returns a finished value and the next continues the computation". If the ruling goes the other way, sonnet-2 is clean on this rule; the Sonnet tier stays violated through sonnet-1. sonnet-2 lines 51-52 each hold one condition and one expression, allowed here as 2026-10-31 held sonnet-1's same lines, and their layout is recorded outside the list.
"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom": no file contains |>, so it is not exercised in 5 of 5.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": 5 of 5 violate, as in 2026-10-31. Topic blocks: opus-1 line 211 describe "the default server" do, the same opus-1 block as 2026-10-31, and haiku-1 line 139 describe "exit of a subscribed process" do, decided by "A block named after a condition, or after a requirement where the project asks for that, still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict" and the case's "when a subscriber exits", not "exits". Two-function blocks: haiku-1 line 33, haiku-2 line 29, sonnet-2 line 72. Test names: haiku-2 lines 30 and 72 "returns :ok"; sonnet-1 line 58 "returns :ok for a pid and for an email" and sonnet-2 line 104 "returns :ok even with no subscribers", which add a condition and still name only the :ok return; sonnet-2 line 223 "publishing after the exit does not crash the server" says only that the call did not fail, counted as 2026-10-31 counted "is fine". Clean: "when a subscribed process exits" in the other four; function-plus-condition blocks at haiku-1 69 and 111. Not counted, as in earlier grades: "fails when :mailer is missing" (haiku-1 25), "requires a :mailer option" (sonnet-1 47), "requires a mailer" (sonnet-2 64), "does nothing for a topic with no subscribers" (haiku-1 105), "to a topic without subscribers does nothing" (sonnet-1 136), "publishing to a topic with no subscribers does nothing" (haiku-2 123), "keeps working after a subscribed pid exits" (haiku-1 172, its body asserts a delivery), "the server keeps running" (sonnet-1 217), "the server survives a subscriber exiting abnormally" (sonnet-2 234, its body asserts the removal).

"Assert with patterns" (unchanged): 4 of 5 violate. Bare matches in test bodies: opus-1 33 (lines 51, 52, 65, 66, 67, 74, 75, 83, 91, 100, 101, 102, 103, 105, 114, 115, 125, 126, 128, 130, 145, 156, 157, 167, 168, 179, 186, 187, 188, 197, 198, 199, 204); haiku-1 1 (line 62); sonnet-2 1 (line 59); haiku-2 and sonnet-1 0. Matches in setup and in the double are outside "In a test body" and are not counted (opus-1 lines 13 and 33, the shape the concurrency rule's own example writes). opus-1 line 176 {dead, ref} = spawn_monitor(fn -> :ok end) cannot fail. sonnet-1 is violated only by line 53 assert is_pid(Process.whereis(server)), the check 2026-10-21, 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 graded violated and 2026-10-31 graded violated when spelled != nil; sonnet-1 is clean if that ruling goes the other way. One-shot assert Process.alive?(...) (haiku-2 126, 184; sonnet-1 141, 224; sonnet-2 231, 239) is not counted here, as in 2026-10-31. No run uses elem/2, puts the expected value on the left of ==, or binds a held value and compares it with == afterwards.

"Wait for messages, not for time" (unchanged): 5 of 5 violate. Process.sleep polling after exits: opus-1 line 255, haiku-1 line 211, haiku-2 line 263, sonnet-2 line 53. sonnet-1 has no Process.sleep; it monitors every exit and calls :sys.get_state after the :DOWN, and is violated only by line 40 assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, _}, decided by "Match the reason too, `:normal`, `:shutdown` or the one the test caused: a `_` there lets a crash for another reason pass.", as 2026-10-22-d graded baseline-opus-1 and baseline-sonnet-1 on the same helper. Other :DOWN patterns: opus-1 177 :normal (a process dead before it subscribes); haiku-1 197 :killed; haiku-2 200 _reason, 242 :killed, 248 :normal; sonnet-1 185 :boom; sonnet-2 180 :killed, 205 _. opus-1 never monitors a subscriber whose exit is under test; sonnet-2 monitors in two of its seven exit tests. Sync calls before refute_received: opus-1 line 245, sonnet-1 lines 129 and 138, haiku-2 line 118, sonnet-2 line 156. One-shot assert Process.alive? is not polling and is not counted.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" (unchanged): 5 of 5 violate. opus-1 line 214 starts the default-named server in an async: true module, despite its comment at line 213, graded as 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22-b graded the same opus shape and 2026-10-31 graded haiku-1's. haiku-1 line 20 starts every test's server under the default name, and line 29 calls start_link. haiku-2 line 225, sonnet-1 line 49 and sonnet-2 lines 59 and 68 call start_link from tests. The default-name tests at haiku-2 lines 212-213 and sonnet-1 line 64 are not counted, because both modules are async: false and those tests are about that default, as 2026-10-22-c and later sweeps treated them. No run calls start_supervised/1 for the start failure. Every subscriber is a bare spawn/1, clean as before.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" (unchanged): 4 of 5 violate. opus-1 is clean: line 21 async: true with a Registry keyed by the server pid, the shape 2026-10-22-b graded clean. Its default-name test in the async module is counted under the start rule and not here, as 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22-b did; 2026-10-31 cited such a test under this rule only for a run that also shared the application env. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 register the test process (lines 19, 21, 26), sonnet-1 routes it through the application env (line 20), and all four set async: false.

"Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours", "Use setup for shared data" and "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" (unchanged) are clean: every double is a module with @behaviour Notify.Mailer passed as :mailer; every setup with data returns a map matched in test heads, except haiku-1, whose setup returns :ok and shares nothing, not exercised as 2026-10-22-c graded the same shape; no test module has a @moduledoc, and use then alias open each body.

Outside the list: haiku-2 lines 51-55 spread an expected list inside an assertion, counted under "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" as 2026-10-31-check counted the same shape. sonnet-2 lines 51-53 break "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line" ("`cond` already carries an expression on the left of each `->`, so its bodies go on the next line unless every one is a short literal or name"). Not counted, as in earlier grades: formatter wraps after == with the expected list on one line (opus-1 69-70 and 136-137, sonnet-1 81-82, sonnet-2 90-91); sonnet-2 lines 29-33, a spread map in a call whose result is bound to a name, which that rule exempts; test support modules without @moduledoc; private helpers above the tests (sonnet-1, sonnet-2); and the section label # Helpers (haiku-2 229).

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3, ten times each: every run passed every time with no warnings (opus-1 20 tests, haiku-1 17, haiku-2 22, sonnet-1 19, sonnet-2 20). mix format --check-formatted passes on all five, confirming format_ok in result.json.
